targets.authors: Milne, G. R., & Boza, M. E.
targets.title: Trust and concern in consumers' perceptions of marketing information management practices.
targets.evidence_quote:
Based on the above discussion, we partially replicate and
extend Milne and Boza's (1999) original findings after two
decades.
targets.outcome_quote:
Although many of
our results are consistent with those of Milne and Boza (1999),
we find shifting relationships. Trust and relationship marketing
activities are still the strongest path for reducing privacy
concern and enhancing direct marketing usage. While trust and
privacy concern have a negative relationship with each other,
paradoxically, privacy concern is not negatively but positively
related to direct marketing usage.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors frame findings as consistent in part with shifted relationships. General discussion explicitly contrasts the original negative privacy concern–usage relationship with the current positive relationship, alongside retained trust effects. This is mixed despite confirmation of the principal trust strategy.

reasoning: Full 22-page article including references; title, DOI and three authors match. New 2017 sample retests one 1999 paper, with additional industries and analyses. Other privacy literature motivates extensions rather than additional original targets. Analyses comparing 1997 and 2017 model estimates do not establish a separate original-data reproduction.
